note: SEC-EDGE-001. A REASON for every entry in docs/edge-rbac-baseline.json, so "open to all roles" stops reading the same whether an entry is deliberate or unexamined. Verdicts: public (the handler never authenticates, so role is a category error), internal (pg_cron, not a user), headless (nothing calls it, so gating decides nothing — AUDIT-024), open-by-design (every tenant member legitimately uses it; row scoping is the real control), needs-gate (a restriction is wanted and is missing — this is the worklist), unexamined (nobody has looked yet, stated rather than implied). check:edge-rbac requires an entry here for every baselined function.

EXAMINED AND FIXED 2026-09-20, and the question here was ROW scope rather than role scope. Every branch resolved its customer as ?customerId= || ?customer_id= || the JWT claim, then checked only that the customer belonged to the caller tenant - on the service-role client, which bypasses RLS. The override is a real feature (_context.ts called it the dealer-staff view) but NOTHING VERIFIED THE CALLER WAS STAFF, and a portal customer is in the tenant too, so that check passed for them and ?customerId=<sibling> returned the sibling dashboard, invoices, equipment and usage. The claim was also read from user_metadata as a fallback, which the session holder writes - the same SEC-TENANT-003 reasoning this file already applied to tenant, one field over. Now: app_metadata only, resolved ONCE after the tenant resolve, a claim-holder asking for a different id gets 403 CUSTOMER_SCOPE_VIOLATION rather than a silent fallback, and a caller with no claim (staff) keeps the override. IMPACT STATED HONESTLY: nothing in this repo sets customer_id on any user, so no portal customers exist yet and the staff branch is what runs today - a door closed before the feature that opens it ships.
